title: P0: Investigate and patch KV slot surface entropy causing cross-tenant GPU OOM cascades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private observed sudden GPU OOM cascades during sustained high-concurrency sessions over the last 72 hours. Root cause analysis points to a previously unseen interaction between the KV cache slot allocation heuristic and the allocator slab rebalancer: under certain traffic patterns (long-lived sessions with heavy prefix caching and irregular eviction patterns) KV slot metadata becomes fragmented and the reclamation path fails to free large pinned pages, causing effective GPU memory pressure and cascading OOMs. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and a runtime patch to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a Dedicated node pool with multi-tenant config and enable session prefix KV caching
2) Run a mixed workload: 70% streaming generation sessions with sequence lengths skewed towards 6-12k tokens per session and 30% short stateless requests
3) Keep sessions pinned (long polling / streaming clients) while repeatedly updating cache entries for those sessions to induce tombstone and slot churn
4) Observe allocator slab fragmentation metrics in Grafana: rising pinned_pages, kv_slot_tombstones, and dropped_evictions
5) Reproduce GPU OOMs after ~8-12 hours under high concurrency (>180 concurrent sessions) as reclaimed pages fail to be released back to the device allocator.
investigation_notes: Initial alert: customer-facing SE reported repeated P95 latency spikes followed by OOM events during an evening traffic ramp (hosted and dedicated clusters).
Heap snapshots show a growing set of pinned KV slot handles in the session allocator that are not reclaimed by the compaction pass.

Race condition found in kv_index_reconcile: when a slot tombstone is added concurrently with a pending prefetch, the slot is marked stale but retain_count is not decremented in the fast path, leaving handles referenced by the kernel pin list.
Allocator interaction: slab rebalancer defers moving large pages under high-copy cost, and combined with above stale handles results in unreachable pinned pages.
Repro script constructed and validated in staging to exercise the race with synthetic long sessions.
mitigation_actions: 1) Applied emergency routing policy to divert traffic from affected Dedicated node pool and scale burst capacity to avoid host-level OOMs (rolled out 2026-03-11 02:12 UTC).
2) Deployed a hotpatch to Hosted that forces aggressive KV tombstone draining every 5 minutes while we stabilize the compactor (hotpatch id: hp/2026-0311-02).
3) For Private customers, provided manual remediation steps and a kube job to run a safe, offline KV compaction.
proposed_fix_summary: Introduce an entropy-aware KV compaction pass and a fast-path decrement for slot retain_count to avoid leaving stale handles. Add a slab rebalancer preemptive unpin for large pages when kv_slot_tombstones exceed threshold. The runtime patch includes: (a) kv_index_reconcile fast-path fix to atomically decrement retain_count in the tombstone path, (b) background entropy compactor that prioritizes heavily-fragmented slot ranges, (c) a temporary safety valve to throttle new prefix caching when fragmentation crosses warning thresholds.
deployment_plan: Stage rollout to Hosted (canary 10% nodes) with runtime-1.19.3-rc1 and increased monitoring for 24 hours.
If stable, expand to Dedicated pools in two waves: non-customer facing pools first, then customer pools with manual approval.
For Private deployments, ship a patch bundle and migration job; provide runbook and coordinate with SEs for maintenance windows.
test_plan: Unit tests for retain_count decrement and tombstone lifecycle.
Integration test with synthetic long-session workload that previously reproduced the leak (1000 sessions, 12-hour run).
Chaos test: simulate concurrent prefetch and eviction to verify no stale handles remain.
Performance regression tests for latency and throughput under normal traffic profile.
postmortem_notes: Contributing factors: heuristic that favored keeping large pinned pages to avoid copy cost; the fast-path in kv_index_reconcile omitted an atomic decrement; lack of a fragmentation SLO that would have triggered preventive throttling earlier.
What went well: routing fallback and hotpatches prevented customer-visible data loss; the staging repro was created quickly and allowed an iterative fix.
Follow-ups: add fragmentation alerting to Console dashboards, create a canary workload for long-session KV churn, and add an escape hatch API to force immediate KV compaction for SRE/SE.
